multiplechoiceresponse.p: When asking a model to generate classroom material, the most important thing to supply is:

choice.div: The context and the source material the output must stay faithful to.
A very long prompt with no source.

div.p: Ground the output in your own lesson and state the learner, level and outcome. Otherwise the model invents a syllabus.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Inside an OpenMAIC classroom, the agents are:

choice.div: The roles participants play — a customer, a peer reviewer, a tutor.

div.p: Agents dramatise the scenario so the lesson content has a situation to live in. The scenario, source material and success criteria are the other pieces.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: The first pass of generated material should be treated as:

choice.div: A draft — raw material to edit, verify and align to the outcome.
Proof that the lesson is finished.

div.p: Generate, then edit. The facilitator's judgement is what turns a plausible draft into teaching material.
